findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If currentBestPath contains user-controlled input, it could lead to OS command injection.
findings.assumptions: The function `printf` is used to print the contents of `currentBestPath`. If the contents of `currentBestPath` are not properly sanitized or validated, they could potentially be used to inject malicious commands.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: If `m->nr_nodes` is very large, it could cause an overflow when multiplying by `sizeof(double)`, `sizeof(int)`, or `sizeof(bool)`, leading to an undersized allocation.
findings.assumptions: The number of nodes in the graph (`m->nr_nodes`) is derived from user input or an untrusted source. If this number is not properly validated, it could lead to memory corruption.

findings.title: Use After Free
findings.trigger: If `currentNodePtr->way_ids[i]` is out of bounds, accessing `wayPtr->node_ids[j]` could lead to a use-after-free error if the memory has been freed.
findings.assumptions: The indices `currentNodePtr->way_ids[i]` and `wayPtr->node_ids[j]` are not properly bounds-checked. If these indices are out of bounds, they could lead to accessing freed memory.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If `tempPath` contains user-controlled input, it could lead to OS command injection if `ssmap_path_travel_time` improperly handles this input.
findings.assumptions: The function `ssmap_path_travel_time` is called with `tempPath` as an argument. If this function does not properly sanitize or validate the input, it could lead to OS command injection.
